scope: Rolling editorial context for canonical physical encounters 1 through 42. Difficulty values are current editorial estimates, not simulated win rates.

competitive_index.note: Battles 1-28 record their truthful legacy 983-team review; future closures query this expanded index and store stable reference IDs.

status_legend.static-pass-runtime-unplayed: Current source satisfies the static bespoke and engine-quality checks, but the encounter has not been confirmed by representative ROM playtesting.
status_legend.needs-retune-runtime-unplayed: The authored encounter is coherent but its current editorial difficulty is below the v2 floor.
status_legend.needs-editorial-revision-runtime-unplaye: Static legality passes, but the encounter needs structural revision before it can close under the v2 doctrine.
status_legend.static-blocked-runtime-unplayed: A static correctness failure blocks closure and runtime difficulty assessment.

identity.memory_hook: The rival mirrors the player's generation with its natural type-counter starter.

entries.primary_player_question: How can the chosen starter beat its own same-generation counter without access to a captured team?
entries.tempo: Open one-on-one preparation check with no forced opener.
entries.intentional_opening: Any branch may attack, use Toxic, or Protect according to the matchup; there is no scripted first turn.
entries.intentional_weakness: The rival has only one Pokemon, no switching resource, and no coverage beyond Return and its Pledge STAB.
entries.first_loss_lesson: Use the starter's legal utility, coverage, or a shop item to change the one-on-one instead of trading neutral attacks.
entries.difficulty_rationale: The one-Pokemon format stays deliberately simple across all 21 starter choices, while the counter-starter's +1 level, Life Orb, perfect IVs, and utility now establish the minimum danger floor.
entries.tuning_knob: Runtime-test representative starter branches before changing the +1 offset; do not add a bespoke lock for individual starter choices.

corpus_search.selection: Set inspiration only; every full team was structurally inappropriate before capture access.

identity.memory_hook: A false Mew created by Zorua's Illusion distracts from the real protected Mew in reserve.

entries.primary_player_question: Can the player identify the false ace, manage its support, and preserve an answer for the real Mew?
entries.tempo: Illusion and Icy Wind pressure into Smeargle redirection and a Nasty Plot closer.
entries.intentional_opening: Zorua appears as the final-slot Mew beside Friend Guard Jigglypuff; neither lead is forced to one move.
entries.intentional_weakness: Zorua, Jigglypuff, and Smeargle are individually fragile, and spread damage bypasses the support geometry.
entries.first_loss_lesson: Break Illusion early and remove the support slot before spending the team's best Dark, Bug, or Ghost answer.
entries.difficulty_rationale: This is the first full-team double and punishes target-selection errors, but its three support pieces are fragile and provide multiple disruption windows.
entries.tuning_knob: Tune Jigglypuff and Smeargle durability or Mew's level before changing the illusion identity.

corpus_search.selection: Zorua, Smeargle, Mew, and Jigglypuff roles adapted from separate random-doubles references; no full import.

identity.memory_hook: Four young Bug Pokemon turn Sticky Web into a real physical-offense plan.

entries.primary_player_question: Can the player deny or route around Sticky Web before Rick's three physical attackers exploit it?
entries.tempo: Web lead into Choice pressure, one setup threat, and a recoil-limited Larvesta ace.
entries.intentional_opening: Focus Sash Dewpider may establish Web while still threatening three attacks.
entries.intentional_weakness: The back line is heavily physical, Web can be denied or ignored, and Rock or Water pressure constrains Larvesta.

revealed_information: Dewpider is the sole Web setter
Karrablast is the only setup user
entries.difficulty_rationale: The Web sequence can snowball against autopilot, while shared physical checks and young base stats keep the encounter readable.
entries.tuning_knob: Tune Larvesta or Anorith's level offset; preserve the juvenile Web identity.

identity.memory_hook: Beginner Pokemon execute two expert doubles waves: fast pressure, then redirection into Belly Drum.

entries.primary_player_question: Which wave should the player disrupt first: Pikachu and Taillow's immediate tempo or Paras enabling Zigzagoon?

entries.first_loss_lesson: Preserve disruption or a Ghost for the second wave instead of spending every answer on the fast lead pair.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Either wave can win quickly, but the dangerous setup is telegraphed and both enablers are vulnerable.
entries.tuning_knob: Tune Paras or Zigzagoon levels and durability; keep the two-wave ordering intact.
